predecessors.name: Safavid dynasty
predecessors.text: the Safavid realm held by Nader as regent since 1732: Iran, Herat and the Caucasus reconquered 1730-1735

successors.name: Qajar dynasty
successors.text: Mashhad and Khorasan, taken by Agha Mohammad Khan in 1796

successors.name: Durrani Empire
successors.text: Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul, Peshawar (1747) and Herat (1750)

ledger.x: 1736: the Ottomans confirm Iranian rule in the Caucasus.
22 January 1736: Nader's assembly on the Mughan plain makes him shah.
Early 1737: Nader's army camps at Kandahar.
1738: Kandahar falls.
1738: the Hotaki are finished at Kandahar.
1738: Bahrain.
June 1738: the campaign against the Mughals opens.
June 1738: Ghazni and Kabul.
November 1738: Peshawar.
20 March 1739: Nader enters Delhi; the massacre begins on 22 March (20,000-30,000 dead).
16 May 1739: Nader leaves Delhi.
May 1739: the war ends with the Indus as the boundary.
May 1739: Sindh, among the lands west of the Indus.
1740: Bukhara submits.
1740: Khiva is conquered.
1741: the Dagestan campaign.

1743: Oman. 'In 1743, he conquered Oman and its main capital Muscat.' The Ahmad bin Said page has Persian forces holding Muscat, and Taqi Khan confirming Ahmad as governor of Sohar and Barka after a nine-month siege.
1743: war with the Ottomans.
1744: Nader makes Erekle II king of Kakheti.
1744: Nader makes Teimuraz II king of Kartli (same sentence).
1745: the Dagestan campaign ends in withdrawal.
September 1746: the Treaty of Kerden ends the war.
1747: the Persians are driven out of Oman.
1747-1748: Bahrain and the Gulf coast pass out of Afsharid hands with Nader's death; the Nader Shah page has Iran losing Bahrain only 'to the House of Khalifa in 1783'.
1747 (bridging): Erekle II's Kakheti is free after Nader's death ('Erekle II later unified eastern Georgia as Kartli-Kakheti'); no date on the page.
1747 (bridging): Teimuraz II's Kartli is free after Nader's death.
1747: Ahmad Shah Abdali founds the Durrani Empire.
June 1747 (bridging): Khiva and Bukhara cease to be Afsharid vassals with Nader's death on 20 June 1747; no page dates the end of their submission.
June 1747 (bridging): as for Khiva.
1748: the state shrinks to Shahrokh's Khorasan.
1750: Ahmad Shah Durrani invades Khorasan.
1750: Herat falls to Ahmad Shah.
Early 1751: the first Durrani siege of Mashhad is abandoned.
1 May 1754: Ahmad Shah marches on Khorasan again.
9 May 1755: Shahrokh 'officially restored as king' by Ahmad Shah; the Afsharid page: 'subjected to the Durranis in the second Durrani campaign, 1754-55'.
1796: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar takes Mashhad.

wars.name: Siege of Kandahar (1737-1738)
wars.outcome: Kandahar, 'the last outpost of the Hotak dynasty', taken in 1738.

wars.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India
wars.outcome: Mughal army beaten at Karnal on 24 February 1739; Delhi sacked 22 March; Nader leaves 16 May 1739, annexing 'all lands west of the Indus' and ceding back the east; 20 million rupees indemnity.

wars.name: Nader Shah's Central Asian campaign
wars.outcome: Bukhara forced to submit and Khiva conquered in 1740; both khanates survive.

wars.name: Nader Shah's Dagestan campaign
wars.outcome: 'Managed to take most of Dagestan' but 'later forced to withdraw'.

wars.name: Persian invasion of Oman
wars.outcome: Nader's forces take Oman and Muscat in 1743; Ahmad bin Said holds Sohar and Barka as a tributary governor and expels the Persians in 1747.

wars.name: Ottoman-Persian War (1743-1746)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Kerden, September 1746: status quo ante bellum; Nader's demand for Ja'fari recognition dropped.

wars.name: Durrani invasions of Khorasan
wars.outcome: Herat lost to Ahmad Shah in 1750; Mashhad besieged until early 1751; Shahrokh restored as king on 9 May 1755 after the second Durrani campaign.

certainty.note: The Caucasus, Indus and Oxus frontiers are military lines; the nearest to treaty lines are the Indus boundary of May 1739 and the Ottoman frontier restored by the Treaty of Kerden (September 1746).
Shahrokh's Khorasan has no surveyed edge and shrinks and recovers under Durrani pressure.
